gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Groovy is friendly and funky, its c almost sealed by a narrow slit, while Noto Sans Ethiopic stays open and tall. Shrink the heading and that playful slit would simply vanish.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-georgian: A narrow slit nearly shuts the c in Groovy, and strokes never vary. Noto Sans Georgian runs open-curved and clean down paragraph after paragraph, its short ascenders keeping lines tidy and easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-glagoliti: Loose and cheeky, Groovy keeps its c almost closed behind a narrow slit. Noto Sans Glagolitic goes the other way, round and open, and that opposition is the pair's whole appeal.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Groovy draws every letter with no stroke contrast, leaving only a narrow slit in the c. And Noto Sans Gothic, a sans-serif with huge drilled-bead counters, opens everything back up.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Groovy brings loosely tracked, funky lowercase with its c nearly shut, while Noto Sans Grantha, a plain sans, flows without a snag. One plays, the other simply gets out of the way.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Noto Sans Gujarati reads clean, its curved strokes stopping short of turning inward. Above it, Groovy keeps one flat stroke with no thin or swollen parts, which leaves the sans body free to be the quiet voice.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-g: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi cuts its terminals back to leave a big gap. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi would read smoothly down a full column, a job Groovy, hairline-free, happily leaves to it.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: A steady line with no pressure variation gives Groovy its funky friendliness, while Noto Sans Gurmukhi, a sans-serif, points terminals outward. Page after page it stays tidy and clean.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Funky and loose, Groovy lets its diagonals carry as much weight as its verticals. Yet Noto Sans Hanunoo, a plain sans with lowercase filling most of the height, brings the calm, and that gap is the draw.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Friendly from the first glance, Groovy gives stems and crossbars one thickness, with a narrow slit in the c. Noto Sans Hebrew, a sans-serif with a dominant midsection, sits beneath it and keeps the page moving.
